The Oyo State Government will on Monday begin verifying property owners affected by the second segment of the Ibadan Circular Road project ahead of compensation payments to eligible claimants. The exercise will cover properties along the corridor from Badeku Village on the Ife-Ibadan axis to the Moniya-Iseyin Road end. The state government announced this in a statement issued in Ibadan on Friday by the Special Adviser to Governor Seyi Makinde on Media, Sulaimon Olarenwaju. It said, “The committee overseeing the verification and compensation process urges affected property owners to attend the exercise with the originals and five photocopies of all relevant documents. “Required documents include: Local Government identification letter or residence permit (for non-Nigerians); survey plan of the property; building/property plan drawings; photographs of the property; land purchase agreement; sworn affidavit obtained from a court or the Ministry of Justice; letter of Power of Attorney issued through the Ministry of Justice (for proxy claims); and five recent passport photographs of the claimant. It advised affected property owners to check their names at the Ministry of Lands, the Office of the New Towns and Cities Development Agency on Subuola Road, Agodi GRA, and the Governor’s Office. The committee also warned property owners against fraudsters posing as government representatives and demanding money to help process compensation claims. It stressed that neither the committee nor the state government had authorised anyone to collect money or offer paid assistance with the verification process. “The verification exercise is free, and all that is required is the presentation of the necessary documents and five photocopies of each,” the statement added. The committee urged affected property owners to disregard anyone requesting payment for assistance with their claims. Ademola Adegbite
